item.title: Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
The image is a photograph of the interior of the St. Emmeram Codex. As per Wikimedia Commons:

This image is in the public domain because under the Copyright law of the United States, originality of expression is necessary for copyright protection, and a mere photograph of an out-of-copyright two-dimensional work may not be protected under American copyright law. The official position of the Wikimedia Foundation is that all reproductions of public domain works should be considered to be in the public domain regardless of their country of origin.

Licensing staff consensus is that because the Codex itself is part of the public domain, then this photograph is part of it as well. As such, it is compliant with CC 3.0.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I love the historical context of this, but the redaction here annoys me to no end. What happened to the composer? Why can't we know how many voices join the choir? Why can't we know what happens at which measures? That must be important for testing personnel to know, yeah? It is likely that the skeleton found with the SCP died of immolation, but why must that be redacted? All of this redaction comes off as pointless. It actively detracts from the quality of the article because it withholds important and interesting information for seeming no in-universe reason. As much as I love the idea, the redactions kill it for me to the point that I actually want to downvote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's interesting, though. Since I've been exploring SCP-012 as much as I have, I'd say that this object is far better written. You can say it's a thing what kills you, and the compulsion when you touch it is a little eye-rolling, but this item has history, purpose, and a much clearer meaning.

I'll be honest. I just upvoted it, and if it were presented today, I'd upvote it still. It doesn't kill everyone. It has parameters, well-defined enough to know how to work with it, but just ambiguous enough to be unsure where the line really is.

If I wanted to show people an example of "do this, not that," then this is a good example.

item.content:encoded:
It mentions only two specific denominations, Roman Catholic and Protestant. I feel like the line about "other" Abrahamic religions and non believers should just be dropped and have the whole thing clarified a little. Anyone touching it starts singing, and any Protestants (including the singer, if applicable) within earshot, line of sight, or whatever criteria, burst into flame when the singing gets to the right part of the piece.

I like it (+1 and all that), but I figure if they have that specific of information already, what I suggested would help clarify that little bit of confusing description. As it is, I just have a bunch of questions. Can anyone trigger the singing by touching it? Do Catholics trigger the singing part? Is it just Protestants who will sing after touching it? Are Roman Catholics the only ones who don't burst into flame? Or are Protestants the only ones who do burst into flame? Etc, etc?

item.title: Some clarity (or experimentaion on category D personel...) needed here I think
item.content:encoded:
This article falls into the old error of categorising Christians as either Roman Catholics or Protestants. Where do Anglicans (either protestants who pre-date the protestant movement and where hostile to it (hence the UK monarch's title of "Defender of the Faith") or Catholics who engaged in Protestation, depending who you ask) fall on this scale? Roman Catholicism is not a synonym of Catholicism.

This is complicated by the article itself that seems to have taken a stance, without actually proving it. If it was inteded for Elizabeth then the opening part shoudl drop the "ie any Protestant Denomination" bit.

Otherwise a really cool SCP, got my Upvote.
